market_mood: Risk appetite is firm: US-Iran diplomacy over the Strait of Hormuz is pulling oil lower and lifting stocks, while AI enthusiasm pushed the Nasdaq to an intraday record. A strong dollar and talk of possible rate hikes are the main offsetting worries, alongside a busy M&A tape.

picks.reason: Oil prices are falling on more Gulf supply and optimism that US-Iran talks could reopen the Strait of Hormuz, which squeezes oil producers' revenue.
Cheaper crude means lower jet fuel costs, a classic second-order benefit for airlines, and calmer Middle East headlines help international travel demand.
Shares jumped on reports of takeover interest, with one analyst putting a buyout value at $25-$26 per share.
The stock rose on a report that Sixth Street is reviving its effort to acquire the insurer.
Piper Sandler cut its price target on worries that networking growth is peaking, and the stock fell about 5%.
Royal Caribbean is near a roughly $3 billion deal for half of Sandals, expanding it beyond cruises into land-based resorts.

watchlist_notes.note: S&P 500 is close to a record as Middle East de-escalation hopes and cheaper oil support sentiment.
Nasdaq 100 hit an intraday record on AI-driven buying, though some traders are trimming tech profits.
Dow is supported by the risk-on tone, but energy and bank weakness could cap gains.
No major company-specific news today; it moves with the broad tech rally.
No major news today beyond the general AI-led tech strength.
A top chip analyst is bullish on Nvidia and unusual options activity is building ahead of upcoming catalysts.
No major news today; benefits indirectly from the broad tech rally.
No major news today aside from ongoing AI-sector optimism.
Mercedes partnering with Wayve on self-driving is a reminder that autonomy competition is widening.
Banks lagged in Europe, and Goldman's reported talks for a $37B credit firm show large-cap banks still hunting deals.
Falling crude on Gulf supply and US-Iran talks is a headwind for oil producers.
A dollar near two-month highs and easing Middle East tension reduce the safe-haven bid for gold.
Chatter about possible rate hikes keeps pressure on long-dated Treasury prices.
